credits: Every clip is cut from the USC Sound Effects Library on archive.org — the Red, Gold and Sunset Editorial collections, digitised by Craig Smith (USC) — plus The Designer's Choice UCS Collection: VOICES (Nicholas Judy). All are released CC0 1.0 Universal (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) per their own archive.org licenseurl. Rifles, submachine guns, ricochets, bullet cracks and mechanism: SSE Library: GUNS. Machine guns: Red Library: Guns Machine (R12-06 single shots, R12-18 bursts, R30-31 'all ambience cut out', R12-16, R12-01). Field guns and tank main armament: Red Library: Guns Artillery (R12-37 and R12-15 are a 75 mm — the Sherman's own gun — plus R12-07, R12-38, R12-36) and SSE Library: GUNS. Explosions and the incoming shell: SSE Library: EXPLOSIONS and Red Library: Explosions. Tanks, tracks and engines: GOLD TAPE 15 Tanks Bulldozers (the M-4 cuts are a Sherman). Footsteps: Red Library Footsteps 1 and 3, SSE Library: FOOTSTEPS. Birds and wind: Red Library Animals Birds, SSE Library: WIND. Wounded and dying men: The Designer's Choice VOICES (modern, full-bandwidth male screams, grunts and crying) with support from Red Library Fights, Red Library Voices Men 1 and 2, SSE Library: VOICES. NO CLIP IN THIS BANK HAS A VOICE IN IT EXCEPT THE FOUR voice.* BANKS, and those carry no words. Takes were chosen from each library's MASTER CATALOGUE, not from filenames, because the names hide things: 'R30-03 Artillery Gun Sequence' is a man shouting 'Ready, Fire!' in Mandarin, 'GUNArtl_squad firing 37mm anti tank guns' has the detachment shouting over it (it was in this bank and is not now), 'R15-49 Man Hyperventilating and Screaming' is 'sort of saying no in the beginning', and 'R16-09 Men Grunting and Shrieking' is 'similar to apes in a fight'. None of those are in the game. Every cut is then screened by tools/audio_speech.py, which finds a human vowel by its harmonic comb in the cepstrum: a cut bound for a gun bank is rejected if it has a voice in it, and a cut bound for a voice bank is rejected if it is too continuously voiced to be a cry rather than a word. No attribution is required under CC0; it is recorded because knowing where a sound came from is worth more than the licence obliges. Several cuts are marked 'from optical' in the source, meaning they were lifted from wartime film soundtracks. Prepared with tools/audio_slice.py, tools/audio_slice2.py, tools/audio_voices.py, tools/audio_recut.py and tools/audio_thin.py: transient-sliced to one-shots (or crossfade-looped for the beds), mono, 44.1 kHz, normalised to -3 dBFS, Ogg Vorbis q5. ALSO, the second bank (round 103, tools/audio_slice3.py): modern full-range recordings from freesound.org, cut into one-shots, loops and windows, levelled and re-encoded (modified).
